newsitem.title: UK: Wilhelmshaven refinery delays restart - traders.
newsitem.headline: Wilhelmshaven refinery delays restart - traders.

text.p: The Wilhelmshaven refinery in Northern Germany is experiencing delays in restarting after a month of scheduled maintenance during which the plant's throughput capacity was to be increased, traders said.
The 185,000 barrel a day refinery, bought earlier this year by the Hamburg-based part of the Louis Dreyfus group, was due to restart earlier this week.
But traders said that crude oil, originally bought for the refinery, was being offered quietly on the market.
"I don't know if they have sold anything yet but they were offering Ekofisk (loading) dates between now and the middle of the month," one North Sea crude trader said.
"They do seem to be struggling a bit (in restarting)," another trader commented.

The plant's managing director, Hans Van Weelden, said earlier in the year that crude throughput capacity at the refinery would be increased by over 20 percent during this maintenance period by the addition of new heat exchanging equipment.
The investment in more energy efficient heat exchanging equipment should raise crude throughput capacity to 10.3 million tonnes per year from the 8.5 million tonnes processed in 1996.
The total investment was expected to be $30 million.
